claims.assertion: The described EpiDoc export retains occurrence IDs but excludes the separately stored linguistic analyses. The paper attributes this partly to incomplete annotation and complex alternatives.

claims.locator: 26 exact ajaxitem source URLs and /item/id pointers in the live projection
claims.assertion: All 26 requested records returned their expected source IDs. Site, hand label, find area and inventory strings agree with the registered derivative for these records. This is a documentary consistency check across versions, not a same-snapshot linguistic crosswalk.

acquisition.endpoint_scope: Official homepage/current news/howto/contact and homepage-linked application script; one bounded set of application-defined ajaxitem requests. No guessed linguistic endpoints, login or bulk crawl.
acquisition.next_delivery: Source-issued bounded observation/phys_word/ling_words package from one declared version, preserving alternatives and missingness; intended-use terms by component.

review_questions: Are the source IDs and literal context fields faithfully projected, with versions kept separate?
Can the source editor supply an annotated bounded package with item.id and phys_word.id from the same version, or identify a documented public route?
Does any proposed alignment preserve alternative analyses, missing/unannotated units, source provenance and the existing blind-field firewall?
remaining_gates: Source-editor delivery of separately linked linguistic analyses and a same-version word crosswalk
Intended-use/component rights confirmation for delivered packages
Independent scholarly validation and the separate graphical baseline
